hero.title: Stop Adding Drives. Start Rebuilding Readiness: The Campus Placement Gap Is a Systems Problem, Not a Pipeline Problem
hero.author: HireKarma Editorial Team

blocks.text: Everyone talks about India's youth dividend. Very few talk about why millions of graduates still leave campus without a job offer — or why placement cells burn out running the same drives year after year with marginally better outcomes.

We've all seen the headlines: India produces over 10 million graduates annually, yet employability surveys consistently report that fewer than half are ready for their first professional role on day one.

As TPOs, recruiters, and students, we feel this gap every time a shortlist falls short, a mock interview exposes a résumé that doesn't match skills, or a placement season ends with strong companies visiting but weak conversion. Here is the hard truth we aren't discussing enough: This isn't a talent shortage problem. It's a structural one.
If we continue to address campus hiring as a "more drives, more companies" game, we've already lost.
Here is why the math simply doesn't add up anymore:
The Reality Check

items: Volume vs. readiness: India adds millions of graduates each year, but industry reports continue to flag a wide skills-to-role mismatch — especially in communication, problem-solving, and role-specific technical depth.

Fragmented placement ops: Most colleges still coordinate drives through spreadsheets, WhatsApp groups, and email chains — creating delays, duplicate data, and zero real-time visibility for TPOs and students alike.
The experience paradox: Recruiters demand "job-ready" candidates, yet many campuses offer only one or two generic prep sessions before the season begins.

Linear human capacity: A single TPO team cannot personally coach thousands of students, track every application, and manage dozens of company relationships simultaneously — yet that is exactly what the system expects.
Wasteful use of student bandwidth: Students spend weeks chasing form links and drive updates instead of building interview-ready skills — low-leverage activity dressed up as "placement preparation."

blocks.text: Why "More Placement Drives" Isn't the Answer
Even if every top recruiter visited every campus, five barriers would remain:

items: Readiness arrives too late: Career preparation is treated as a pre-season sprint, not a continuous journey. By the time drives begin, gaps in résumés, communication, and domain skills are already baked in.
Disconnected ecosystems: Students, colleges, and companies operate on different tools with no shared context — applications, shortlists, and feedback live in silos.

The coordination tax: TPOs spend disproportionate time on logistics (scheduling, reminders, offer tracking) instead of strategy (employability mapping, employer relationship building, outcome analytics).

One-size-fits-all preparation: Generic aptitude tests and group discussions don't prepare a CS graduate for a product role or a mechanical engineer for a core manufacturing interview — yet most prep remains undifferentiated.
Placement without persistence: When the season ends, support stops — leaving unplaced students without structured pathways, curated opportunities, or daily placement momentum.

blocks.text: A Shift in Perspective
Maybe the real question isn't "How do we invite more companies to campus?"
It's: "Why are we still expecting manual coordination and last-minute coaching to close an ecosystem-scale problem?"
The solution isn't just more drives or more training sessions. It's about rethinking how the campus hiring system handles readiness, coordination, matching, and follow-through — end to end.

When résumé feedback is continuous, not cosmetic; when drives run on a single platform instead of fifteen inboxes; when AI-matched opportunities reach students daily instead of once a semester; and when a virtual placement cell keeps momentum alive after the formal season — institutions can deliver far more outcomes than headcount alone would suggest.
How HireKarma closes the loop
This is exactly why HireKarma built a portfolio of purpose-built platforms — not another generic job board, but an architecture where readiness, recruitment, and outcomes connect natively:

items: SolviqAI — AI-powered résumé analysis, skill assessments, and mock interviews that prepare students for real hiring rounds before companies arrive.
Disha — End-to-end placement management for colleges: drive scheduling, company coordination, offer tracking, and TPO analytics in one place.
Lakshya — A campus hiring ecosystem connecting students, universities, and recruiters to run drives, manage applications, and shortlist faster.
Shortlisted — India's first AI virtual placement cell: curated batches, AI-matched jobs, and a human coordinator focused on placement every day — not just during season.

blocks.text: We truly believe TPOs and students should spend their bandwidth on high-impact work — building employability, nurturing employer relationships, and converting opportunity into offers — not on manual coordination across disconnected channels.
The gap isn't going away. It's time we stop trying to fill it with more drives and start closing it with better architecture.
